mission_scope: MRMPO analysis of Albuquerque Metro Planning Area transit, parks, healthcare and grocery accessibility for environmental-justice populations; Albuquerque is the substantive urban focus.
specific_albuquerque_connection: Mapped Albuquerque census tracts, southwest Albuquerque and southeast Central Avenue park-access gaps, bus-stop walksheds and transit contours for Albuquerque hospitals/groceries.
exclusion_test: This is spatially resolved Albuquerque transportation-equity analysis, with quantified access differences and named local gaps; it exceeds generic regional jurisdiction or background context.
information_density: Five tabs: Environmental Justice Communities; Walking Access to Open Space; Walking Access to Transit; Transit Access to Healthcare; Transit Access to Groceries. Each renders local thematic layers and policy narrative. The rendered open-space tab compares 55 percent/62 percent ten-minute access; transit tab reports 34 percent five-minute and 58.5 percent ten-minute access. These are source historical analysis figures, not current service statistics.
unique_public_information_value: Readers can inspect neighborhood distribution of benefits and gaps, connect low-income/minority populations to access and understand transportation-investment priorities. Interactive tract popups and spatial overlays add detail beyond a planning document summary.
currentness: Current public live interface. Official MRCOG parent explicitly relates the analyses to Connections 2040. Environmental Justice Priority Tracts item explicitly sources 2016-2020 ACS (evidence-38); app modified May 1 2025. No current analysis refresh date displayed; route/facility currency is unverified. Recommend as historical planning analysis delivered through a live app.
